title: iris × pallide-caerulaea
intro: Iris × pallide-caerulaea, commonly known as the pale blue iris, is a hybrid plant in the iris family, derived from the cross between Iris pallida and Siberian iris (Iris siberica). The pale blue iris has been used in traditional medicine for its health benefits, which include its anti-inflammatory, antibacterial, and antiviral properties, making it effective in treating various health conditions. The therapeutic actions of Iris × pallide-caerulaea include its ability to reduce inflammation, promote wound healing, and exhibit sedative effects. The bioactive constituents of the pale blue iris include iridoids, flavonoids, and phenolic acids, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.
